defects.description: handle() records the message id before applying it, so when the store throws the redelivery is reported as a duplicate and the event is lost.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import {OrderConsumer} from "./src/consumer.js"; import {OrderStore} from "./src/store.js"; const s=new OrderStore(); let fail=true; const orig=s.apply.bind(s); s.apply=(o,st)=>{ if(fail){fail=false; throw new Error("db down");} orig(o,st); }; const c=new OrderConsumer(s); const m={id:"m1",orderId:"o1",version:"1",status:"placed"}; try{c.handle(m)}catch{} console.log(c.handle(m));'

defects.why_missed: The suite redelivers only messages that were applied; no test makes the store fail and then redelivers.

defects.description: handle() compares revisions as strings, so revision "9" arriving after "10" is not stale and overwrites the newer state.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import {OrderConsumer} from "./src/consumer.js"; import {OrderStore} from "./src/store.js"; const s=new OrderStore(); const c=new OrderConsumer(s); c.handle({id:"m10",orderId:"o1",version:"10",status:"shipped"}); console.log(c.handle({id:"m9",orderId:"o1",version:"9",status:"paid"}));'

defects.why_missed: The out-of-order test uses single-digit revisions, where string and numeric order agree.
